title: Tropic sorghum: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Tropic sorghum: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Tropic sorghum is a sorghum variety from Pacific Seeds. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Tropic is a registered sorghum variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1983. Pacific Seeds bred it. It takes 90 to 95 days from planting to harvest, with 4.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Compare it with the others in our [sorghum variety finder](/crop-varieties/sorghum), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for corn and grains](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** 90 to 95 days from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 4.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Tropic sorghum takes 90 to 95 days from planting to harvest. That is 10.7 days faster than the average of the 3 sorghum varieties with a day count, 103.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 4.6 t/ha trails the average of its group, 5.07. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It was weak against anthracnose, rust, grav leaf spot, so scout for them from the early weeks. Read up on [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose).

The pests and diseases that hit sorghum fields most often: [Rice birds (maya)](/pests/rice-birds), [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Tropic sorghum
Sorghum stands drought better than corn, so it fits the dry season and dry uplands. Pick by use: grain for food and feed, or sweet sorghum for juice and syrup.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 90 to 95 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 4.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Tropic?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
